item.title: Fourier Transform-Based Computation of Two-Electron Four-Center Coulomb Repulsion Integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.12608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a Fourier-based method for evaluating two-electron four-center Coulomb repulsion integrals over Slater-type orbitals. Spherical Fourier-Bessel coefficients of the convolution factors are precomputed and reused. Since the spherical part of the integral can be evaluated directly, there remains only a one-dimensional quadrature problem in the radial direction. For the ten reference integrals reported here, the largest absolute discrepancy is $1.7\times10^{-9}$. A preliminary resident-cache benchmark computes approximately $4.2\times10^5$ unique integrals per second on an NVIDIA V100 at the contraction stage.
item.dc:creator: William Chen, Lior Silberman, Ury Segal, Chen Greif

item.title: Median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo for nested integration
item.description: arXiv:2610.12643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nested integrals $\int f\left(\int g(\boldsymbol{y},\boldsymbol{x})\mathrm{d}{}\boldsymbol{x}\right)\mathrm{d}{}\boldsymbol{y}$ where $\boldsymbol{y}\in[0,1]^{d_1}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}\in[0,1]^{d_2}$ frequently arise in Bayesian experimental design, medical decision making, and computational finance. Statistical estimators for nested integrals are more computationally demanding than for standard integrals. Recent studies demonstrate that the median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (mRQMC) method achieves super-polynomial convergence rates for analytic integrands. We extend mRQMC methods to nested integrations and propose a novel double-loop mRQMC estimator with super-polynomial convergence rate if both the inner and outer integrands are analytic. Established estimators for nested integrals, such as double-loop or multilevel Monte Carlo, are by contrast limited to algebraic convergence rates. However, expected information gain (EIG) applications from experimental design typically do not fulfill this condition due to a lack of regularity in the outer integrand. We address this through a theoretically-grounded importance sampling regularization scheme. Although super-polynomial convergence rates remain achievable for the inner integral, only the algebraic rate $\alpha+3/2-\epsilon$ for any $\epsilon>0$ can be theoretically guaranteed for the outer integral in the EIG, where $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$ denotes the order of the mixed derivatives of the regularized outer integrand. Our approach shows substantial improvements over double-loop randomized quasi-Monte Carlo methods based on the sample mean in moderately high-dimensional settings for a simple polynomial example. Moreover, we demonstrate improved convergence behavior of the median-based estimator for the more challenging setting of EIG estimation.
item.dc:creator: Arved Bartuska, Yang Liu, Ra\'{u}l Tempone

item.title: Variational neural transport for aggregation-diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a neural transport framework for nonlinear, nonlocal aggregationdiffusion equations arising in chemotaxis, polymer dynamics, and related applications. Based on the Onsager variational principle, we reformulate the governing equation as a constrained optimal control problem, taking the velocity field as the control and evolving the density via the associated continuity equation. The velocity field is parameterized by a neural network trained on the variational objective evaluated along particle trajectories. By coupling the density and generalized score equations into a single system solved via the Euler method, the score function propagates efficiently for loss evaluation. Furthermore, we establish a rigorous error analysis that decomposes the total error into approximation, optimization, Monte Carlo sampling, and time-discretization components, and prove corresponding error bounds. Numerical experiments across several representative models demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed approach.
item.dc:creator: Qianyi Li, Hailiang Liu

item.title: A kernel-independent precorrected-FFT method
item.description: arXiv:2610.12821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The precorrected-FFT has been used to rapidly evaluate $N$-body sums arising in electromagnetics and acoustics settings. It has, however, been historically limited to kernels that satisfy a Green's identity. In this work, we demonstrate that, using an improved version of the method of proxy points, the precorrected-FFT can be used to efficiently compute $N$-body sums with a wide variety of kernels. This algorithm requires no analytic information beyond pointwise access to the kernel. Our examples include kernels from non-local PDEs, Matern kernels, anisotropic kernels, and the Green's functions of high order PDEs. We also provide a detailed algorithm for choosing the proxy points and spreading grid, as implemented in the new pcfft package. We show these algorithmic choices result in favorable scaling when compared to other kernel-independent fast summation methods. Finally, we use the algorithm to accelerate a wide variety of integral equations solvers involving non-standard kernels, with applications in surface scattering, geophysics, and microbial community formation.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Goodwill, Owen Melia

item.title: Riemannian Hessian analysis of Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.12833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem are Riemannian gradient descent methods on the sphere under a metric induced by a discrete elliptic operator. We analyze their convergence through the condition number of the Riemannian Hessian at the ground state. Bounds of the Rayleigh quotient of the Riemannian Hessian give a uniform analysis of these methods for different metrics. The uniform analysis applies to the classical metrics, such as the shifted Laplacian and the energy-adaptive metrics. Inspired by this analysis, we also consider three new metrics. One of them is a Thomas--Fermi metric, whose condition number is bounded uniformly in the interaction strength for the one-dimensional harmonic trap and whose iteration count does not grow in the Thomas--Fermi regime in the numerical tests. The performance suggested by our analysis is consistent with three-dimensional numerical tests with up to one billion unknowns, for both Riemannian gradient descent and Riemannian conjugate gradient methods, whose practical performance is also related to the Hessian condition number. The Thomas--Fermi flow needs the fewest iterations, while the metrics inverted exactly by tensor-product solvers are the fastest in computational time on one GPU card.
item.dc:creator: Shixin Zheng, Xiangxiong Zhang

item.title: Numerical Smoothness and Error Analysis for Evolution Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is a lecture note to introduce the innovative concept of numerical smoothness and its application in the error analysis of numerical solutions of evolution equations. We start from the two fundamentally different error splittings. One splitting is popular, which brings us to local error defined along the original solution and error propagation by numerical schemes. The well know Lax Equivalence Theorem is based on this error splitting. The other splitting can only be seen in a few numerical ODE books, which brings us to local error defined along the numerical solution and error propagation by the solutions of the evolution equations. The innovative concept of numerical smoothness arises from the second error splitting. While there are many difficulties when we use numerical stability in error analysis of nonlinear evolution equations, we will show that numerical smoothness works naturally in error analysis/estimation/control with advantages in several ways. We will define temporal and spatial numerical smoothness indicators, prove the necessity of the boundedness of these indicators for having optimal convergence rate, and show computable error estimates as functions of these smoothness indicators. Moreover, these error estimates are optimal in the approximatons' convergence rates and also optimal in the error propagation of the evolution equation. In comparison with error analysis framework of the Lax Equivalence Theorem, from the necessity results and the error estimates proven in the numerical smoothness framework, we have a new equivalence theory: Consistency + Numerical Smoothness <=> optimal error estimates. Unlike the Lax Equivalence Theorem, the new equivalence theory works well for nonlinear problems, nonlinear schemes, and many other complications of problems.
item.dc:creator: Tong Sun

item.title: Linear and entropy-stable scheme for the dynamic van der Waals model of non-isothermal liquid-vapor flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.13029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a linear and decoupled fully discrete scheme that preserves the entropy production property for the dynamic van der Waals model. This model provides a thermodynamically consistent diffuse-interface framework for describing non-isothermal phase transitions in single-component liquid-vapor systems, containing the coupled conservation laws of mass, momentum and energy. We first introduce an equivalent reformulation of the governing equations that avoids the use of chain-rule identities, which generally fail under discrete differentiation. Further, a component-wise convex-splitting method is employed to calculate the discrete chemical potential and temperature. This treatment provides a discrete entropy-stable inequality without a time step restriction. Based on the explicitly treated velocity, the scheme allows the three conservation equations to be solved linearly and sequentially in a decoupled manner. Since the momentum equation does not directly affect the entropy-stability analysis, we use a classical linear semi-implicit scheme to solve it. Numerical experiments verify the expected numerical accuracy. Simulations of droplet evaporation and two- and three-dimensional Leidenfrost effects further demonstrate the proposed method can capture complex non-isothermal phase-transition dynamics while numerically reproducing the discrete entropy production behavior.
item.dc:creator: Yunzhuo Guo, Zhonghua Qiao, Xianmin Xu

item.title: Numerical Stability of Extended-Domain Spectral Collocation: Floating-Point Regularization and an Equilibrium Law for the Frame Constants
item.description: arXiv:2610.13222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extended-domain spectral collocation expands the solution of a boundary value problem in the Laplacian eigenbasis of an enclosing box and collocates at as many nodes as modes. The square system is exponentially ill-conditioned, and the impossibility theorem for equispaced data rules out stable geometric convergence; yet such solvers converge geometrically to a few orders of magnitude above the unit roundoff. We explain why in one dimension. The collocation solution is the solution operator applied to the interpolant of the data in an operator-dependent test space whose Lebesgue constant must grow exponentially for geometric convergence, so exact solutions can amplify data errors exponentially. In floating-point arithmetic the error of any coefficient vector is bounded by its nodal residual, its distance to a competitor and two frame constants, a leakage and a restricted Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund constant, bounded uniformly in the number of modes at a fixed positive threshold; for a backward-stable solve, under a condition on the perturbed matrix, the bound is uniform in the conditioning for suitably analytic data and, with computed constants, within a factor of about ten of the error floor of a direct solver. For the Poisson operator the rate of the two constants along the tail of the spectrum is given by a constrained equilibrium problem of logarithmic potential theory. For an interval of length $L$ extended by $\delta$ at each end, the problems for $\delta$ and $L^2/(4\delta)$ are dual, the rate is linear for $\delta = L/2$, and it starts with slope minus the fraction of the extended domain occupied by the extension, so for $\delta < L/2$ the leakage constant obeys no power law with the exponent of the end of the spectrum. In experiments, convection--diffusion operators behave like the Poisson operator at moderate P\'eclet numbers.
item.dc:creator: Po-Yi Wu

item.title: ADER-ZIST - a mixed explicit ADER-DG and zonally implicit space-time DG approach for Cartesian cut cell meshes
item.description: arXiv:2610.13245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present high order accurate mixed explicit-implicit discontinuous Galerkin (DG) schemes for the solution of hyperbolic systems of conservation laws on Cartesian cut cell meshes. Such meshes may contain arbitrarily small cut cells, which leads to the well-known small cell problem: the CFL condition of explicit schemes would severely restrict the admissible time step. To overcome this difficulty, we use high order explicit fully-discrete one-step ADER-DG schemes only on Cartesian cells away from the embedded boundaries. The zone close to the embedded boundary, which consists of cut cells and their direct face neighbors, is discretized with an implicit space-time DG scheme that is coupled to the explicit scheme directly via the numerical flux. The resulting scheme, called ADER-ZIST (ADER-DG with Zonally Implicit Space-Time DG), is conservative by construction, and its time step is determined only by the size of the Cartesian background cells. Curved embedded boundaries are represented by high order isoparametric sub-triangles inside the cut cells, and the nonlinear system of the implicit cells is solved via an inexact matrix-free Newton-Krylov method. For problems with shock waves, we add an artificial viscosity term whose strength is controlled by an oscillation-eliminating smoothness sensor. ADER-ZIST is assessed on a comprehensive set of test problems for the compressible Euler equations, ranging from smooth flows around straight and curved embedded boundaries to acoustic scattering and shock-dominated flows. The scheme essentially reaches its nominal order of accuracy N+1 for smooth solutions and for polynomial degrees up to N=5, on meshes with minimal volume fractions of the small cut cells down to the order of 10^-7.
item.dc:creator: Michael Dumbser, Christian Engwer, Sandra May, Peter Munch

item.title: On the Convergence of the Mesh-Free Discretization of a Non-Linear Bond-Based Peridynamic Model with a Bond-Breakage Criterion
item.description: arXiv:2610.13355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show the convergence of a commonly used mesh-free discretization of a dynamic non-linear bond-based peridynamic model with irreversible damage implemented via a bond-breakage criterion for a fixed horizon $\delta >0$. The model chosen here is a mathematically well-posed regularization of a discontinuous peridynamic operator often found in the literature, which assumes that fracture results from strain in tension only. We explicitly include the one-point quadrature used in this scheme in the analysis. The convergence is with respect to the natural norm of the solution space given by $C^1([0,T],L^\infty(\Omega)^d)$, and therefore $L^\infty(\Omega)^d$ in the spatial coordinates. This result heavily constrains the spatial regularity of the continuous solution which we prove afterwards. More specifically, for locally $L$-Lipschitz continuous input data, local Lipschitz bounds are derived for the displacement, regardless of damage. This is consistent with interpreting the peridynamic model used here as an approximation to a truly discontinuous fracture model with a length-scale parameter given by the horizon $\delta>0$. We note that we do not deal with the limit of the solutions as $\delta \searrow 0$.
item.dc:creator: Lukas Pflug, Michael Stingl, Max Zetzmann

item.title: Global Optimization of Beam Profiles for Suppressing the Bump-On-Tail Instability
item.description: arXiv:2610.13391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A particle beam with constant intensity that propagates into a plasma triggers a bump-on-tail instability. It has been demonstrated that beam modulation can be used to significantly reduce this instability. However, finding the optimal beam profiles that accomplish this is a complex optimization problem that suffers from an extremely rugged optimization landscape and a relatively high-dimensional parameter space. In this paper, we evaluate a number of optimization algorithms and find that population based methods (in particular, CMA-ES and Differential Evolution) perform best. In particular, we investigate beam profiles where the beam is either completely turned ON or OFF. This configuration is easier to accomplish experimentally, but leads to a higher-dimensional and thus more challenging optimization problem. We obtain ON/OFF beam profiles that reduce the instability by more than 80% and thus perform significantly better than what has been reported in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Sandro Mignelli, Lukas Einkemmer

item.title: Regularisation and Parameter Choice Rules for Composite Linear Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we propose a novel regularisation strategy for structured linear inverse problems of the form $Ax=F \circ G x = z$. Instead of using the operator $A$ or a complex scheme involving both $F$ and $G$ simultaneously, combining already existing and simpler regularisations for $F$ and $G$ allows the use of established and optimised programs for high-speed computations. As classical parameter choice rules fail in the scenario when no source conditions are known because intermediate error bounds may be unavailable, we provide both a-priori and a-posteriori rules with a convergence speed analysis given source conditions. We test the proposed method on the pre-clinical medical imaging technique of magnetic particle imaging with different choices of regularisation and on a convolution problem for an analysis of the convergence speed.
item.dc:creator: Christina Brandt, Patrick Horn

item.title: On a maximum principle in discretization with spherical harmonics
item.description: arXiv:2610.13540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spherical harmonics have been studied extensively and are used in many fields of application. We consider the probably earliest application of spherical harmonics, namely for a representation of the solution of the Laplace equation on the $d$-dimensional unit sphere where the boundary data are represented in a spherical harmonics basis. We consider general $d \geq 2$. For the solution $u$ of the Laplace equation the fundamental maximum principle holds. If one approximates the boundary data in the finite dimensional space spanned by all spherical harmonics of degree at most $N$, the resulting discrete solution, denoted by $u_N$, does in general not satisfy the maximum principle. In this paper we derive sharp estimates for $r_N^{\rm max}$ such that the maximum principle holds for $u_N(x)$ for all $x \in \Bbb{R}^d$ with $\|x\| \leq r_N^{\rm max}$. We show that for $d=3$ one has $r_N^{\rm max} \gtrsim 1- 3 N^{-1} \ln\big( 2^\frac13 N \big) $. Similar estimates are derived for $d \neq 3$. We also study the sharpness of these estimates.
item.dc:creator: Arnold Reusken

item.title: Preconditioning proximal Galerkin: mesh and degree robust solvers for variational inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.13591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The proximal Galerkin algorithm is a structure-preserving solver for variational inequalities that results in discretization-independent nonlinear iteration counts. However, in large three-dimensional simulations, the arising Newton saddle point systems cannot be feasibly solved by direct methods. To leverage an iterative linear solver, we propose a robust and scalable block preconditioner. Instead of using the usual dual Schur complement that acts on the latent variable, we design a preconditioner for the primal Schur complement. This leads to a block preconditioner that requires two approximate inverses of the latent block and only one of the primal Schur complement. The latent block represents an algebraic equation which, after a small perturbation, can be cheaply inverted. We then introduce two choices of approximations for the primal Schur complement: a PDE-operator-based and an algebraic approach. Either approximation can be efficiently inverted by geometric multigrid. We investigate the effectiveness of these strategies when proximal Galerkin is applied to obstacle, Signorini, and strain-constrained elasticity problems and also compare with a monolithic multigrid approach. Choices of standard relaxation methods, in the block preconditioner route, lead to robust iteration counts with respect to the mesh size and discretization degree. Moreover, in the context of the Signorini, specialized relaxation and prolongation also result in effective solvers for nearly-incompressible elastic materials. The linear solves are parameter-robust in 2D, with only mild growth in 3D. This allows for the solution of a three-dimensional contact problem, with a Poisson's ratio of 0.499, discretized with over ten million degrees of freedom.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis P. A. Papadopoulos, Pablo D. Brubeck

item.title: Energy conserving compatible space--time FEM for deterministic and stochastic rotating shallow water
item.description: arXiv:2610.13624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a fully discrete energy conserving discretisation of the rotating shallow water equations with arbitrary order in space and time. A space time finite element discretisation is used, built from compatible finite element methods in space and continuous Petrov-Galerkin schemes in time. Projected auxiliary variables for Hamiltonian derivatives are necessary for exact energy conservation. We provide an iterative solver approach based on monolithic patch smoothers, which allows us to efficiently converge a Newton method sufficiently that energy errors due to the solver are very small. We extend this construction to the energy conserving Stochastic Forcing by Lie Transport formulation. Then we demonstrate the convergence, conservation and robustness in numerical tests.
item.dc:creator: Maneesh Kumar Singh, Colin J. Cotter

item.title: Analysis of an inexact Schwarz domain decomposition method in 3D
item.description: arXiv:2610.13793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider an inexact version of the Schwarz domain decomposition method in $3$D to solve a Laplace problem in a domain that is the union of two overlapping spheres. We solve each subproblem approximately by projecting its boundary data $L^2$-orthogonally onto the space of spherical harmonics of degree at most $N$. The model problem arises from the ddCOSMO solver used for implicit solvation in computational chemistry. We analyze the Schwarz-spherical domain decomposition method by establishing a new variant of the maximum principle.
item.dc:creator: Nibedita Ghosh

item.title: Fast and Stable Arbitrary Precision Approximate Matrix Multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2610.13905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present several new and surprising results on the theory and practice of Arbitrary Precision Approximate (APA) matrix multiplication, which refers to algorithms that output merely approximations to matrix multiplication even in exact arithmetic. While APA algorithms have been around for nearly half a century, and despite the fact that they have potentially lower (asymptotic) cost than many fast exact matrix multiplication schemes, they have not been studied as closely, to the extent that relatively little is known about their numerical properties. In this paper, we shine a spotlight on these algorithms by presenting three important results. First, we provide a new search algorithm for APA routines that is easy to use, automatically generates encoding matrices with functional entries, and can match or beat the best known APA algorithms for several sizes. In particular, we improve the upper bound on the border rank of $\langle 2,4,5 \rangle$ matrix multiplication. Second, we combine this insight with alternative bases to minimize the number of additions in an APA algorithm, thereby improving its leading coefficient. Finally, we prove the same kind of stability that characterizes fast exact matrix multiplication for an algorithm of Bini [Calcolo 1980] that computes an exact product of two matrices using a modified APA scheme (with or without alternative bases).
item.dc:creator: Ioana Dumitriu, Olga Holtz, Abraham Hsu, Nicholas Liskij, Yoav Moran, Ryan Schneider, Oded Schwartz, Shuncheng Yuan

item.title: Mesh-Native Tokenisation: Retrofitting Foundation Models to Unstructured Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.12618v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics foundation models are an increasingly popular approach for building versatile emulators for spatiotemporal systems. They require tokenisation layers that lift physical field data into a latent representation suitable for dynamic processing. A typical choice for this layer is a convolutional encoder, which lifts field information in a locality-aware way and can be trained very efficiently. However, this choice cannot be applied to a large class of scientific computing problems where data are represented on unstructured meshes, for example simulations on domains with curved boundaries. Such data typically require graph neural network architectures, which are more expensive to train and, in the form currently used, encode information differently from their CNN counterparts, thus limiting the portability of physics emulators between these data regimes. In this work we introduce Mesh-Native Convolution (MNC), a locality-aware tokenisation layer that encodes unstructured mesh-based data in a way that is analogous to CNNs. This approach leads to models that can be trained once on mesh data and then deployed to arbitrary unstructured meshes, even if these are irregular, with minimal retraining. We show that this tokenisation approach can be used to retrofit grid-pretrained foundation models efficiently on unstructured meshes and provide theoretical results to confirm the consistency of this approach with classical CNN encoders. We demonstrate the favourable performance of this retrofitting approach, which in many cases reaches acceptable accuracy even in zero-shot deployment, and outperforms existing baselines after only a few epochs of fine-tuning, thus providing an efficient bridge between the two data regimes.
item.dc:creator: Georg Maierhofer, Miles Cranmer, Payel Mukhopadhyay

item.title: Symbolic-Permutation-Based Direct Sparse Jacobian Assembly for Accelerated Power-Flow Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.12654v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The repeated assembly of the sparse Jacobian matrix constitutes a primary computational bottleneck in the Newton-Raphson power-flow analysis. Through an algebraic equivariance analysis of the Jacobian matrix, this paper proposes a direct sparse Jacobian assembly method based on symbolic permutation. By pre-applying the permutation to the admittance matrix during a one-time symbolic phase, the runtime bus-type projection overhead is entirely eliminated. Consequently, complex Jacobian differentiation and global matrix assembly fuse into a single operation, yielding a single-pass, branchless algorithm that streams values directly into contiguous memory. The framework is realized in the open-source RustPower solver. Benchmarks on IEEE test systems and PEGASE 9241 demonstrate that the proposed assembly is 24.4-30.1x faster than the MATPOWER- style baseline and 6.0-7.8x faster than the Schafer-Braun optimized assembly. End-to-end, the grid-level solve time is 11.7x-154.3x faster than pandapower 3.5.4 with Numba, while leaving numerical results and convergence behavior unchanged. Compared with the native C++ LightSim2Grid 1.0.0, grid-level performance is comparable on IEEE 39 and 1.3x-1.8x faster on IEEE 118 and the PEGASE systems. The method extends directly to general problems where a sparse Jacobian inherits its structure from a static network operator, including transient stability analysis, EMT simulation, and OPF Hessian assembly.
item.dc:creator: Tianshi Cheng, Venkata Dinavahi

item.title: A Framework for Arbitrary-Order Electromagnetic Field Approximation Based on Analytical Solutions of Maxwell's Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12682v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The standard Yee finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm uses Maxwell's equations to replace first order temporal derivatives with spatial curls. In this work, the relation is extended to arbitrary orders: a Time-Space Theorem establishes the correspondence between higher-order temporal derivatives and successively higher-order spatial curl operators. Based on this relation, an arbitrary-order framework for electromagnetic field approximations is developed. The framework constructs higher temporal orders through higher curl orders and permits different spatial discretizations and curl-estimation techniques, thereby providing a general basis for developing numerical algorithms of arbitrary orders. As one implementation, an arbitrary-order FDTD algorithm is constructed using staggered time and space stepping together with recursive curl estimations. Numerical simulations of an initial-value problem are performed for temporal approximation orders from second to tenth order while the spatial and temporal step sizes are kept fixed. Comparisons with the analytical solution show that the errors decrease rapidly and monotonically with increasing approximation order. These results demonstrate the practical potential of the framework for high-accuracy electromagnetic computation and provide a basis for further development of arbitrary-order numerical methods.
item.dc:creator: David Wei Ge

item.title: Polyconvex neural-network surrogates with learned paired directional features for anisotropic hyperelastic homogenization
item.description: arXiv:2610.12801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Approximating the effective anisotropic hyperelastic response of a representative volume element (RVE) requires constitutive expressiveness, mechanical consistency, and computational efficiency. This work develops a polyconvex physics-augmented neural network (PANN) construction based on paired directional features whose orientations, stretch powers, and determinant exponents adapt to the RVE response. The features are composed with convex, componentwise nondecreasing cores, realized as an input-convex neural network (ICNN) or an input-convex Kolmogorov-Arnold network (ICKAN). The complete energies satisfy objectivity, an exactly stress-free reference, two-dimensional polyconvexity, and prescribed growth conditions by construction, and nonnegative energy is certified separately for the selected models. On a multicavity and a single-cavity periodic cell, these energies are compared with an Unconstrained energy, trained identically without the curvature and growth constraints, and with three hyperreduced projection-based reduced-order models (HPROMs), which serve as physics-based references. On the first cell, learning the features lowers the stress error sevenfold, and six features suffice on both. The constrained energies remain below one percent in stress error and in the displacement error of a tensile-coupon FE$^2$ application with a full-order reference, whereas the Unconstrained energy and the HPROMs are more accurate inside the data. Beyond the data, however, the Unconstrained energy loses rank-one convexity, and under confined compression it stops below half of the 500 MPa that the constrained energies reach. These results quantify what the guarantees cost in accuracy and what they secure beyond the data.
item.dc:creator: S. Ares de Parga, A. Cornejo, J. A. Hern\'andez, R. Rossi

item.title: Block encoding of semiseparable matrices via their generators
item.description: arXiv:2610.13228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an explicit quantum circuit that constructs a block encoding of a generator-representable semiseparable (one-pair) matrix directly from its two generators. For an $N\times N$ semiseparable matrix with $N=2^{n}$, the circuit uses $2n+2$ ancilla qubits and has $O({\rm polylog} N)$ depth, and it realizes a $(2\sqrt{N},\,2n+2,\,2 \sqrt{2}\ \varepsilon)$-block encoding, where $\varepsilon$ is controlled by the accuracy of the state-preparation routines that load the generators. The building blocks of the circuit are cyclic shifts, swaps, and Hadamard gates, each admitting an efficient implementation through the binary decomposition of the relevant indices.
item.dc:creator: Giacomo Antonioli, Gianna M. Del Corso, Roel Van Beeumen

item.title: Sustainable Cloud-Fog-Edge Systems for Smart Buildings: Algorithmic Adaptation under Memory Constraints and Dynamic Orchestration Strategies
item.description: arXiv:2610.13307v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The escalating environmental footprint of the Information and Communication Technol- ogy (ICT) sectorwith global Data Center electric- ity usage potentially reaching 3% by 2030 and the imperative for real-time responsiveness in smart buildings demand a foundational shift towards Edge Computing. This article proposes a holis- tic architectural and algorithmic approach for cre- ating autonomous, resilient, and privacy-preserving learning systems within smart buildings, advancing the core concept of the building itself as the data center. Our contributions, demonstrating originality compared to conventional centralized systems, are structured around three main pillars: 1) Validation of resilient data acquisition chains using the af- fordable Arduino ecosystem (Uno R4 WiFi/BME280) and secure persistence solutions including centralized archiving (Node-RED/MySQL) and secure remote transfer (Python/rsync/SSH). 2). The proposal of a lightweight, KOptim orchestration framework, inter- operable with the FIWARE standard, for the dynamic management of Service Level Agreements (SLA). 3) The adaptation and experimental valida- tion of the Generalized Hebbian Algorithm (GHA) for Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on low- power microcontrollers,We introduce and compare an iterative learning strategy using data buffers, featuring sorting and explicit preservation of extreme samples to maintain diversity. Experimental results on the high-dimensional Tour Perret sensor data confirm that this novel method, despite introducing a necessary temporal complexity of O(W log W ) due to sorting, achieves convergence and final result quality that is visually equivalent to processing the entire dataset in full memory, reliably identifying two distinct operational states.
item.dc:creator: Mamadou Sow, Christophe Cerin

item.title: An inverse spectral problem for the wave equation with a varying Robin parameter at the boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.13629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An inverse spectral problem for a $(1+1)$-dimensional wave equation with wave speed $c(x)$ is considered. The spectral data consist of the eigenvalues of the Neumann--Dirichlet problem for the operator $-c^2(x)\partial_x^2$ together with their derivatives with respect to a Robin parameter at the boundary. We propose a two-step recovery procedure. In the first step, the Neumann-to-Dirichlet map $\Lambda$ is reconstructed from the spectral data using the results of arXiv/0406582. In the second step, the reconstructed $\Lambda$ is used within the regularization strategy for the boundary control method presented in arXiv:1509.04478. As an improvement, the regularization of the control problems employs a weighted combination of $L^2$ and $H^1$ penalty terms, and we prove a uniform convergence result for the family of optimal controls, thereby allowing the regularization parameters to be tuned simultaneously. We also prove that the forward spectral map, which assigns to a wave speed its spectral data, is Lipschitz continuous, and that the inverse spectral map underlying the reconstruction procedure is H\"older continuous on a subclass of wave speeds. The method is implemented numerically and validated on both smooth and piecewise smooth wave speed profiles. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the recovery of the wave speed exhibits high accuracy and robustness.
item.dc:creator: Antti Hannukainen, Petr Kulikov, Matti Lassas, Lauri Oksanen

item.title: Diffraction of waves by finite thin coatings: asymptotic expansion and effective models
item.description: arXiv:2610.13680v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the Helmholtz equation in a Dirichlet angular sector (which may be locally perturbed) covered on one side by a thin homogeneous layer. First, we propose an asymptotic expansion of the solution at any order and for any angle when the thickness of the layer tends to 0, using a matched asymptotic expansion. This consists in introducing different asymptotic expansions in three subdomains -- the vicinity of the corner, the layer and the rest of the domain -- that are linked through matching conditions. The presence of the corner makes these matching conditions delicate to derive because the fields have complex singular behaviors. We overcome this difficulty using a novel system of algebraic tools, including formal series and operators on these series. Moreover, we justify the asymptotic expansion with error estimates and provide details on the form of the expansion depending on the angle. We numerically validate this expansion up to order 5. This requires computing the behavior at infinity of some corner profiles. To do this, we introduce a Galerkin-type method enriched by complements at infinity. These complements are known functions that appear in the behavior at infinity of the corner profiles with coefficients that become unknowns of the system. Finally, we propose effective models of order 3, resp. 5 where, far from the corner, the layer is replaced with an effective Robin, resp. Ventcel, boundary condition and, near the corner, an artificial boundary is introduced and a Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) type condition is imposed. The DtN map relies on a modal decomposition of the truncated asymptotic expansion at order 3, resp. 5. The modes take into account the singular behavior of the expansion terms, the corner profiles and some algebraic matching coefficients. We prove the well-posedness of our effective models, as well as error estimates, and provide numerical results.
item.dc:creator: C\'edric Baudet

item.title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.13804v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gaussian process solvers for linear partial differential equations (PDEs) return posteriors rather than point estimates, but they condition only on equality information: the PDE residual, boundary data, and measurements. Many solutions of interest also obey inequality constraints, including nonnegativity, monotonicity, and absence of arbitrage, which equality conditioning cannot enforce. We prove that conditioning a Gaussian process prior jointly on linear equality observations and a finite-dimensional inequality event is equivalent to conditioning sequentially in terms of Borel measures on the solution space. The physics-informed posterior is therefore a valid prior for the inequality update at virtual points. The combined law is non-Gaussian yet computable through truncated-Gaussian moments, and neither the PDE conditioning nor the inequality update requires modification. We evaluated the construction on a Poisson benchmark, option-price surfaces, and air-quality fields. Under incomplete boundary data, a monotonicity constraint lowered the error of a two-dimensional Poisson reconstruction by $63\%$. On a real S&P 500 option chain thinned to $20$ retained quotes, no-arbitrage constraints reduced held-out extrapolation error by $22\%$ and cut the calendar-arbitrage rate from $10\%$ to $1\%$. On four real air-quality snapshots, nonnegativity reduced a Gaussian moment-based sub-zero-tail proxy by $74\%$ at the sparsest monitor count. Changes in mean accuracy and constraint diagnostics differed across data regimes. The probability of the noisy virtual constraint event under the equality posterior measures agreement with the specified bounds before the update. The construction turns admissibility from a post-processing step into conditioning information for probabilistic PDE solvers.
item.dc:creator: Boyuan Deng, Kshitiz Upadhyay, Michael Shields

item.title: High order integration of stochastic dynamics on Riemannian manifolds with frozen flow methods
item.description: arXiv:2503.21855v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a new class of numerical methods for solving stochastic differential equations with additive noise on general Riemannian manifolds with high weak order of accuracy. In opposition to the popular approach with projection methods, the proposed methods are intrinsic: they only rely on geometric operations and avoid coordinates and embeddings. We provide a robust and general convergence analysis and an algebraic formalism of exotic planar Butcher series for the computation of order conditions at any high order. To illustrate the methodology, an explicit method of second weak order is introduced, and several numerical experiments confirm the theoretical findings and extend the approach for the sampling of the invariant measure of Riemannian Langevin dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Eugen Bronasco, Adrien Busnot Laurent, Baptiste Huguet

item.title: Convergence analysis of GMRES applied to Helmholtz problems near resonances
item.description: arXiv:2505.16345v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The finite element solution of Helmholtz problems near resonant or quasi-resonant frequencies poses significant challenges, as iterative solvers typically suffer from severely degraded convergence. We analyze the convergence behavior of GMRES applied to linear systems arising from such configurations. Theoretical convergence estimates are derived based on harmonic Ritz values, highlighting their proximity to small eigenvalues as a key determining factor. We further examine deflation strategies and their interplay with preconditioning techniques, using the Complex Shifted Laplacian preconditioner as a case study. Numerical experiments on resonant and quasi-resonant test cases validate the theoretical framework and demonstrate the effectiveness of deflation strategies. This study provides new insights and practical guidance for analyzing and improving iterative solvers for time-harmonic problems near resonances.
item.dc:creator: Victorita Dolean, Pierre Marchand, Axel Modave, Timoth\'ee Raynaud

item.title: A general framework for the OSRC-preconditioned EFIE in computational electromagnetics
item.description: arXiv:2507.20707v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate on-surface radiation condition (OSRC) preconditioners for the electric field integral equation (EFIE), considering Electric-to-Magnetic (EtM) and Magnetic-to-Electric (MtE) approximations applied from both the left and the right. A pseudodifferential analysis establishes the well-posedness of the four resulting formulations and shows that, locally, the OSRC EtM and MtE approximations present a similar structure to the EFIE itself and its inverse, respectively. At the discrete level, both MtE formulations are compatible with the standard RWG/SNC discretization and can be implemented without barycentric refinement, whereas the EtM formulations require an appropriate discrete duality map and BC/RBC spaces. Numerical experiments show that the OSRC preconditioners substantially improve GMRES convergence compared with the unpreconditioned EFIE, with the refinement-free MtE formulations also providing the lowest computational cost among the formulations considered.
item.dc:creator: Ignacia Fierro-Piccardo

item.title: An inherent regularization approach to parameter-free preconditioning for nearly incompressible linear poroelasticity
item.description: arXiv:2507.22334v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An inherent regularization strategy combined with block Schur complement preconditioning is investigated for linear poroelasticity problems discretized using the lowest-order weak Galerkin method in space and the implicit Euler scheme in time. At each time step, the resulting saddle point system becomes nearly singular in the locking regime due to the near incompressibility of the solid. The regularization arises from an inherent identity in the original system, preserves the exact solution, and ensures nonsingularity. For the regularized systems, standard inexact block Schur complement preconditioning is shown to be effective, and preconditioned MINRES and GMRES methods exhibit convergence essentially independent of the mesh size and locking parameter -- in terms of both convergence factors and asymptotic error constants. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions confirm the robustness of the regularization strategy and the effectiveness of the block preconditioners with respect to mesh size and locking for the regularized systems.
item.dc:creator: Weizhang Huang, Zhuoran Wang

item.title: Learning Hidden Ecological and Epidemic Processes in a Reduced-Order Space
item.description: arXiv:2601.09811v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study data-driven learning of ecological and epidemic dynamics governed by nonlinear reaction and reaction--diffusion systems. We consider both neural approaches for learning the underlying reaction dynamics from trajectory data and Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) for discovering sparse, interpretable governing equations. A key component of this work is a partial-learning framework for reaction--diffusion systems. The prescribed diffusion operator is projected onto a reduced-order space and explicitly retained during differentiable integration, while only the unknown local eco-epidemic reaction is learned. This enables efficient training on fine spatial grids by evaluating the neural reaction only at a small set of informative nodes. The reduced solution is then reconstructed on the original fine grid and evaluated over both the training interval and an unseen future prediction horizon. Finally, the learned neural reaction is processed by SINDy to recover a sparse, interpretable symbolic model of the underlying dynamics. Experiments with clean and noisy data demonstrate high predictive accuracy, implicit denoising, computational efficiency, and the ability to recover sparse reaction models.
item.dc:creator: Maria Vasilyeva, Zheng Wei, Kelum Gajamannage, Hyangim Ji, Aleksei Krasnikov, Alexey Sadovski

item.title: A Fourier spectral method for the cutoff Boltzmann equation: Convergence analysis and numerical simulation
item.description: arXiv:2603.26220v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work presents a novel Fourier spectral method for the cutoff spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation with Maxwellian and hard potentials. We establish finite-time error estimates in a weighted whole-space $L^2$ norm, with explicit dependence on the velocity cutoff $R$ and the number of Fourier modes $N$.
item.dc:creator: Yanzhi Gui, Ling-Bing He, Liu Liu

item.title: MVNN: A Measure-Valued Neural Network for Learning McKean-Vlasov Dynamics from Particle Data
item.description: arXiv:2604.00333v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Collective behaviors that emerge from interactions are fundamental to numerous biological systems. To learn such interacting forces from observations, we introduce a measure-valued neural network that infers measure-dependent interaction (drift) terms directly from particle-trajectory observations. The proposed architecture generalizes standard neural networks to operate on probability measures by learning cylindrical features, using an embedding network that produces scalable distribution-to-vector representations. On the theory side, we establish well-posedness of the resulting dynamics and prove propagation-of-chaos for the associated interacting-particle system. We further show universal approximation and quantitative approximation rates under a low-dimensional measure-dependence assumption. Numerical experiments on first and second order systems, including deterministic and stochastic Motsch-Tadmor dynamics, two-dimensional attraction-repulsion aggregation, Cucker-Smale dynamics, and a hierarchical multi-group system, demonstrate accurate prediction and strong out-of-distribution generalization.
item.dc:creator: Liyao Lyu, Xinyue Yu, Hayden Schaeffer

item.title: An asymptotic-preserving reduced-order method for parametrised rarefied gas flow by proper generalised decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2607.10085v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modelling rarefied gas flow using the Boltzmann equation is vital in many areas. Because of the high dimensionality and coexistence of multiple characteristic scales, conventional solution strategies for this equation incur prohibitively high computational costs and are inadequate for rapid response in engineering design simulations. Based on proper generalised decomposition (PGD), we propose an a priori, asymptotic-preserving reduced-order method for the high-dimensional parameterised Shakhov kinetic model equation. Separated representations reduce the kinetic problem to a set of low-dimensional problems. We incorporate synthetic equations into the PGD iteration so that, in the hydrodynamic limit, the iteration reduces to solving the Navier-Stokes equations, whose solution naturally exhibits a low-rank structure. Furthermore, treating the rarefaction parameter as an additional coordinate yields a solution over the whole range of rarefaction in one offline computation. It enables fast online queries to any point in the parameter space. Numerical examples using this method show reasonable precision and a significant reduction in computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Luowei Yin, Wei Su

item.title: AlgMortar: a fully algebraic multiscale mortar preconditioner
item.description: arXiv:2607.22905v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The solution of large-scale symmetric positive definite (SPD) linear systems arising from discretizations of second-order elliptic equations is challenging, especially in applications with highly heterogeneous coefficients, such as flow in porous media, which can lead to severely ill-conditioned systems. In this context, multiscale methods have recently been used to accelerate Krylov subspace methods, owing to their favorable parallel scalability. In this work, we present AlgMortar, a fully algebraic realization of the Multiscale Mortar Mixed Finite Element Method (MMMFEM). The method uses only information extracted from the fine-grid system matrix, which facilitates its implementation in existing solvers. AlgMortar uses graph partitioning to define a domain decomposition directly from the matrix graph. On each subdomain, it builds local linear systems that mimic Dirichlet problems, and couples the resulting local solutions through an algebraic interface condition that recovers the weak flux-continuity mechanism of MMMFEM. We prove that the method is well posed when the matrix is SPD. Numerical experiments on fine-grid linear systems arising from finite-volume discretizations of Darcy flow problems show that, when used as a preconditioner for the conjugate gradient method, the proposed approach exhibits good scalability and is competitive with state-of-the-art algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods for challenging heterogeneous, high-contrast test cases, including highly irregular corner-point grids. Additional tests with SPD matrices arising from problems other than finite-volume discretizations of Darcy flow showed competitive performance with AMG.
item.dc:creator: Luan F. Santos, Fabricio S. Sousa, Roberto F. Ausas, Rafael T. Guiraldello, Felipe Pereira

item.title: Second-Order Accuracy from Large Local Errors in Interface Problems: A Discrete Green's Function Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2608.30020v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Finite difference methods for interface problems often exhibit large local truncation errors near the interface, particularly when discontinuities in coefficients or solution derivatives are present. Nevertheless, many such schemes achieve second-order accuracy, a phenomenon not fully explained by standard pointwise consistency arguments. In this work, we provide a precise explanation of this behavior through the structure of the discrete Green's function associated with the underlying conservative difference operator. An explicit representation of the Green's function reveals a two-plateau structure in its weighted increments. By expressing the numerical error in terms of this Green kernel, we show that the dominant interface truncation errors, although individually of order \(O(1)\), possess a cancellation structure that reduces their effective contribution to the global error. The exact Green's-function analysis leads to a class of conservative interface flux--balance schemes for which the cancellation mechanism yields second-order accuracy in the maximum norm. The weighted harmonic discretization is included as a particular member, and its cancellation property is established directly. For Cartesian grids with a flat interface parallel to a coordinate direction, the same conservative cancellation mechanism persists along grid lines crossing the interface. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions directly illustrate the predicted cancellation behavior and the resulting second-order accuracy. These results demonstrate that second-order accuracy in interface problems can arise from the interaction between localized truncation errors and the global structure of the discrete operator, rather than from pointwise consistency alone.
item.dc:creator: So-Hsiang Chou, Patrick Nyadjo Fonga

item.title: Sum of Squares and Non Sum of Squares Regimes for the Toeplitz Bottcher Wenzel Form
item.description: arXiv:2610.08980v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Toeplitz matrices are among the simplest structured models of translation invariance, arising naturally in convolution, stationary covariance models, and discretizations of translation-invariant operators. For a pair of real matrices, the B\"ottcher--Wenzel form (BW form) is a nonnegative quartic measuring the gap in the corresponding commutator inequality. L\'aszl\'o conjectured that, when both matrices are Toeplitz, this quartic is a sum of squares for every matrix order. We show that the conjecture is false. More precisely, we identify an explicit family of corner-supported Toeplitz pairs, retaining only the outermost diagonals on the two sides, for which the associated BW form is not a sum of squares at all sufficiently large orders. The proof reduces the complete family of Gram representations to a finite complex test: its Gram-invariant part develops a strictly negative limiting direction, while the remaining Gram-dependent contribution vanishes. We also give an explicit sufficient threshold for the matrix order. The negative result is complemented by two positive regimes. If either Toeplitz factor is symmetric or skew-symmetric, then the corresponding BW form is SoS for every order, with the other factor allowed to be an arbitrary real Toeplitz matrix. For unrestricted Toeplitz pairs, we further prove SoS representability for every $2\le N\le50$, with formal Lean~4 verification through order 20. The large-order non-SoS theorem, including the explicit sufficient threshold, has also been formally verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Wenqi Zhu, Ping Nie

item.title: Analysis and Detection of Stagnation in Floating-Point Summation
item.description: arXiv:2610.10819v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stagnation in the summation of floating-point numbers occurs when the running sum, or the accumulator, does not change its value despite addends being greater than zero. Here we define different types of stagnation - commonly referred to as swamping or absorption, where one operand in an addition is nearly or completely rounded off---in floating-point summation, and propose algorithms for detecting it in numerical code that uses floating-point arithmetic. Whilst cancellation in floating-point arithmetic has been studied, for example by Lam et al. in `Dynamic floating point cancellation detection', stagnation has not been exploited as a property for detecting and reporting accuracy loss in floating-point operations. We have built prototype dynamic stagnation detection tools in two languages, MATLAB and Julia, and applied them to applications ranging from basic summation of a vector, to matrix multiplication, to a fluid flow simulation model. With this tool, users are able to identify areas of their floating-point code where stagnation occurs - in those areas of the code one may need to switch to a higher precision number format, apply stochastic rounding, or use different summation algorithms such as compensated summation. To the best of our knowledge we provide a first rigorous definition of stagnation in floating-point summation.
item.dc:creator: Mantas Mikaitis, William Woolfenden

item.title: Linearized Wasserstein dimensionality reduction with approximation guarantees
item.description: arXiv:2302.07373v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce LOT Wassmap, a computationally feasible algorithm to uncover low-dimensional structures in the Wasserstein space. The algorithm is motivated by the observation that many datasets are naturally interpreted as probability measures rather than points in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and that finding low-dimensional descriptions of such datasets requires manifold learning algorithms in the Wasserstein space. Most available algorithms are based on computing the pairwise Wasserstein distance matrix, which can be computationally challenging for large datasets in high dimensions. Our algorithm leverages approximation schemes such as Sinkhorn distances and linearized optimal transport to speed-up computations, and in particular, avoids computing a pairwise distance matrix. We provide guarantees on the embedding quality under such approximations, including when explicit descriptions of the probability measures are not available and one must deal with finite samples instead. Experiments demonstrate that LOT Wassmap attains correct embeddings and that the quality improves with increased sample size. We also show how LOT Wassmap significantly reduces the computational cost when compared to algorithms that depend on pairwise distance computations.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Cloninger, Keaton Hamm, Varun Khurana, Caroline Moosm\"uller

item.title: The Riemannian Convex Bundle Method
item.description: arXiv:2402.13670v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the convex bundle method to solve convex, non-smooth optimization problems on Riemannian manifolds of bounded sectional curvature. Each step of our method is based on a model that involves the convex hull of previously collected subgradients, parallelly transported into the current serious iterate. This approach generalizes the dual form of classical bundle subproblems in Euclidean space. We prove that, under mild conditions, the convex bundle method converges to a minimizer. Several numerical examples implemented using Manopt$.$jl illustrate the performance of the proposed method and compare it to the subgradient method, the cyclic proximal point algorithm, as well as the proximal bundle method.
item.dc:creator: Ronny Bergmann, Roland Herzog, Hajg Jasa

item.title: Butcher series for Hamiltonian Poisson integrators through symplectic groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2503.05000v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We exhibit a new pre-Lie algebra in the framework of symplectic groupoids and, in turn, use Butcher trees to compute the Taylor series of a solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation on any symplectic groupoid $\mathcal{G} \rightrightarrows M.$ The impact of this new algebraic approach is twofold. On the geometric side, it yields algebraic operations to approximate Lagrangian bisections of $\mathcal{G}$ using the Butcher-Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra and, in turn, aims at a better understanding of the group of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of $M.$ On the computational side, we define a new class of Poisson integrators for Hamiltonian dynamics on Poisson manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Busnot Laurent, Oscar Cosserat

item.title: PySymmetry: A Sage/Python Framework for the Symmetry Reduction of Linear G-Equivariant Systems
item.description: arXiv:2509.19479v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Despite the prevalence of symmetry in scientific linear systems, these structural properties are often underutilized by standard computational software. This paper introduces PySymmetry, an open-source Sage/Python framework that implements classical representation theory to simplify G-equivariant linear systems. PySymmetry uses projection operators to generate symmetry-adapted bases, transforming equivariant operators into a more efficient block-diagonal form. Its functionalities include defining and reducing representations, calculating multiplicities, and obtaining the explicit block structure. We demonstrate PySymmetry's versatility through three case studies: a chemistry application, a numerical benchmark on the non-Hermitian Schr\"odinger equation that achieved a performance increase of over 17x compared to standard methods, and a symbolic investigation that enabled the first complete analytical classification of a challenging problem in celestial mechanics. Designed for seamless integration with libraries like NumPy and SciPy, PySymmetry offers a powerful, user-friendly tool for exploring symmetries in theoretical and applied contexts. ```
item.dc:creator: Leon D. da Silva, Marcelo P. Santos

item.title: Approximation of differential entropy in Bayesian optimal experimental design
item.description: arXiv:2510.00734v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bayesian optimal experimental design provides a principled framework for selecting experimental configurations that maximize obtained information. In this work, we consider settings where the likelihood entropy is independent of the design or can be evaluated explicitly, which applies, e.g. to additive noise models with design-independent or explicitly computable noise entropy. This reduces the problem to maximum entropy estimation, where the nested integral defining the expected information gain collapses into a single integral. Our study is motivated by large-scale inference problems, such as inverse problems, where the computational cost is dominated by expensive likelihood evaluations. Under additive Gaussian noise model, we propose a computational approach in which the evidence density is approximated by a Monte Carlo or quasi-Monte Carlo surrogate, while the differential entropy is evaluated using standard methods without additional likelihood evaluations. We prove that this strategy achieves convergence rates that are comparable to, or better than, state-of-the-art methods for full expected information gain estimation, particularly when the cost of entropy evaluation is negligible. Our approach relies only on mild smoothness of the forward map and avoids stronger technical assumptions required in earlier work. We also present numerical experiments, which confirm some of our theoretical findings.
item.dc:creator: Chuntao Chen, Tapio Helin, Nuutti Hyv\"onen, Yuya Suzuki

item.title: Exact analytical PGSE signal for diffusion confined to a cylindrical surface using a spectral Laplacian formalism
item.description: arXiv:2603.23421v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Objective. To derive an exact analytical expression for the diffusion MRI signal arising from diffusion confined to a cylindrical surface under finite rectangular pulsed-gradient spin-echo (PGSE) gradients, and to develop computationally efficient strategies for repeated model evaluations. Approach. The Bloch-Torrey equation was solved using a spectral matrix formalism of the Laplace operator in the eigenbasis of the cylindrical surface. The resulting signal is expressed as a product of non-commuting matrix exponentials and is valid for arbitrary rectangular gradient durations and separations, without approximations to the diffusion propagator or spin phase distribution. A reduced real spectral basis was introduced to decrease the dimensionality of the problem. Accelerated implementations based on Strang splitting and Gauss-Legendre quadrature were developed for repeated signal evaluations and computation of the spherical mean. The analytical signal was validated against Monte Carlo diffusion simulations. Main results. The exact formulation showed excellent agreement with Monte Carlo simulations over a wide range of cylinder radii and acquisition parameters. The spectral expansion converged rapidly with mode order, and the reduced basis substantially decreased computational cost without loss of accuracy. The accelerated implementations provided large additional speed-ups while retaining controllable errors relative to the exact solution. Significance. The proposed framework extends exact finite-pulse solutions of the Bloch-Torrey equation to diffusion confined to cylindrical surfaces and provides practical implementations for directional and orientationally averaged diffusion MRI signals. It therefore offers an approximation-free reference for assessing faster signal approximations and for applications requiring large numbers of model evaluations.
item.dc:creator: Erick J Canales-Rodr\'iguez, Chantal M. W. Tax, Juan Manuel G\'orriz, Derek K. Jones, Jean-Philippe Thiran, Jonathan Rafael-Pati\~no

item.title: Differentiable Hybrid Modelling for Learning and Optimising Chemical Transport Processes from Experimental Data
item.description: arXiv:2609.04011v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Transport models underpin the design and optimisation of chemical processes, yet their constitutive laws are typically hand-picked, their experimental initial conditions are assumed exact, and their computational cost restricts optimisation to a handful of process variables. Here we introduce a differentiable hybrid modelling framework that embeds neural networks within a GPU-accelerated population balance equation solver to discover constitutive laws and assimilate initial conditions directly from experimental crystallisation data. Using thirteen real experiments with multi-dimensional size and shape measurements, we show that treating measured initial conditions as exact yields a physically inconsistent rate law despite improved predictive accuracy, whereas assimilating them recovers a physically consistent, non-linear law and reduces trajectory error sevenfold relative to conventional modelling. End-to-end differentiability further enables gradient-based optimisation of high-dimensional operating profiles, identifying a 300-variable temperature profile that reduces crystal aspect ratio by 25% at constant mass, facilitating superior product attributes. Our framework augments, rather than replaces, mechanistic modelling, offering a general route to learning transport models from data and optimising processes with them.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Jessop, Mohammed Alsubeihi, Ben Moseley, Ashwin Kumar Rajagopalan

item.title: asdex: Automatic Sparse Differentiation in JAX
item.description: arXiv:2610.12336v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many tasks in scientific computing and machine learning require the Jacobian or Hessian matrix of a function. Automatic differentiation (AD) computes these derivatives to machine precision, but materializing a dense $m \times n$ Jacobian requires $n$ forward-mode or $m$ reverse-mode AD passes, one per column or row. For a large class of functions, each output depends on only a few inputs, making the derivative matrix sparse. Automatic sparse differentiation (ASD) exploits this structure in four steps: detection of the input-agnostic sparsity pattern, coloring of a graph to group columns or rows that can share an AD pass, compressed differentiation to compute a compressed derivative matrix with one AD pass per color, and finally decompression into the original sparsity pattern. The number of colors, and hence of AD passes, is often independent of the problem dimension: a banded Jacobian with $b$ contiguous bands, for instance, only ever requires $b$ colors, regardless of its size. asdex offers the first standalone ASD toolkit in the popular JAX ecosystem. With $\texttt{asdex.jacobian}$ and $\texttt{asdex.hessian}$, it provides sparse drop-in replacements for $\texttt{jax.jacobian}$ and $\texttt{jax.hessian}$.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Hill, Guillaume Dalle
